# Abhidhammamātikāpāḷi (Tika Abh09t)

**ID:** Tika Abh09t
**Section:** Tīkā Abhidhammamātikāpāḷi (tika-abh09)
**Collection:** Tika-Abhidhamma
**Title (Pali):** Abhidhammamātikāpāḷi
**Title (English, from literature):** Table of Contents of the Abhidhamma
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Abhidhammamātikāpāḷi* (also titled *Abhidhamma-mātikā*) is an Abhidhamma text catalogued in the Tīkā section of the Chaṭṭha Saṅgāyana collection [Nyanatusita 2008]. It functions as a compendium bringing together the *mātikā*s (matrices, registers, or tables of contents) from all seven canonical books of the Abhidhammapiṭaka: the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, *Vibhaṅga*, *Dhātukathā*, *Puggalapaññatti*, *Kathāvatthu*, *Yamaka*, and *Paṭṭhāna* [Nyanatusita 2008; Walker 2018]. In regional Buddhist performance and manuscript cultures, particularly in Southeast Asian leporello manuscripts, excerpts from these seven opening sections were standardized as communal recitation scripts utilized in protective and funerary rituals [Walker 2018].

Automated analysis by DharmaNexus reflects this structural synthesis, identifying 114,743 text-reuse matches across 742 Pali texts, with no cross-language parallels registered [DharmaNexus]. Its heaviest overlaps correspond directly to canonical Abhidhamma passages and their primary commentaries, prominently including the *Puggalakathā* of the *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 1.1), the *Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Kusalattika* of the *Paṭṭhāna* (Patthana 1.2), the *Khandhavibhaṅga* of the *Vibhaṅga*, and multiple chapters of the *Yamaka* (such as the *Suddhacittasāmañña*, *Anusayavāra*, and *Uppādavāra*), alongside the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi-aṭṭhakathā* and *Visuddhimagga* [DharmaNexus].

In the bibliographical tradition, several related exegetical works and expansions are documented, including an expanded version designated as the *Abhidhammamātikā-vitthāra*, the *Mātikā-sarūpa-vibhāvinī*, the *Chāyārāma-pakaraṇa* (or *Mātikatthakathā*), and an aṭṭhakathā known as the *Tīkā-lvan* [Nyanatusita 2008].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Puggalakathā (Kv 1.1) (§180_2–223_1 ↔ §13.7–40.3); Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā (Atk Abh03a) (§2389_1–2394_7 ↔ §563_2–572_7); Suddhacittasāmañña (Ya 8.2.1) (§2575_4–2579_4 ↔ §98.1–116.1); Kusalattika (Patthana 1.2) (§2678_2–2678_9 ↔ §102.1_0–104.1); Vibhaṅga-aṭṭhakathā (Atk Abh02a) (§1929_8–1933_4 ↔ §990_8–994_4); Dhammasaṅgaṇi-aṭṭhakathā (Atk Abh01a) (§1256_5–1257_12 ↔ §838_0–839_0); Visuddhimaggo (Dutiyo bhāgo) (Anya E0102n) (§1929_8–1933_4 ↔ §1288_8–1293_4); Anusayavāra (Ya 7.2.1) (§2535_5–2537_2 ↔ §84.1_0–102.1)

**Sources**

- [Nyanatusita 2008] Bhikkhu Nyanatusita, Reference Table of Pali Literature (2008) — Identifies the text as a compilation of the mātikās of all seven canonical Abhidhamma works and notes related commentaries and expansions.
- [Walker 2018] Trent Walker, Unfolding Buddhism: Communal Scripts, Localized Translations, and the Work of the Dying in Cambodian Chanted Leporellos (2018) — Explains the contents as excerpts from the beginning of the seven Abhidhamma treatises and describes its ritual and manuscript use.
- [DharmaNexus] DharmaNexus text-reuse database — Provides alignment statistics showing pervasive reuse with the seven Abhidhamma treatises and their commentaries.
